_about: PRO rewrite pass 7: era-2 scenes 79-117 in play order.

scenarios.title: The Second Car
scenarios.text: You buy a second car on a whim after a good week, a convertible in a color the salesman called 'victory'. Then you realize you haven't driven the first one in a month.

choices.label: Sell one of them
choices.result: One of them goes back on the market by Friday, at a loss. You feel smarter for it, and a little silly every time you see a convertible.

choices.label: Give the old one to {sibling}
choices.result: The old car, keys and all, goes to {sibling}, who cries in the driveway and then honks the horn for ten straight seconds.

choices.label: Keep both cars
choices.result: Both stay. They sit side by side in the driveway, shining, and the insurance bill makes you laugh out loud in a bad way.

scenarios.title: The Contract Rumors
scenarios.text: Rumors say the club might not re-sign you next spring. A radio host says it, then a blog, then the guy who makes your sandwich at the deli near the facility.

choices.label: Answer with your leg
choices.result: No interviews, no reading, just kicking every day. The rumors get quieter by November, and the deli guy apologizes with a free sandwich.

choices.label: Ask the club directly
choices.result: A direct question to the general manager, in his office. The answer is honest and incomplete: they love you, and they're keeping options open.

choices.label: Talk it over at home
choices.result: A long evening at home, talking it through, agreeing not to look at houses in other cities yet. It helps more than any answer would.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Elections
scenarios.text: The players' union asks you to run for team representative. The last rep was traded the week after a tense meeting with management, and everybody remembers.

choices.label: Run for the job
choices.result: Elected, by a lot. Now the young players call you about everything, from pensions to parking, and management knows your name in a new way.

choices.label: Nominate someone better
choices.result: A teammate better suited to the job gets your nomination and your vote. He wins, does it well, and thanks you at the end-of-season dinner.

choices.label: Stay off the ballot
choices.result: Off the ballot. You have enough meetings already, and you'd rather spend the time on the field and with family.

scenarios.title: The Mid-Career Injury
scenarios.text: A torn muscle in practice, on a routine kick, with a sound you've only heard other people make. It's the first serious injury of your career, right in your prime.

choices.label: Follow the rehab exactly
choices.result: Every step of the rehab, exactly as written, for ten weeks. It's slow and dull, and you come back whole, which the trainers call rare.

choices.label: Push the timeline
choices.result: Early, by three weeks. You're back on the field and not quite right, and you kick carefully all season, favoring the leg.

choices.label: Lean on the people at home
choices.result: The worst weeks, spent leaning on home: {parent} on the phone every night, {sibling} visiting with bad movies. It gets you through.

scenarios.title: The Rehab Partner
scenarios.text: You're rehabbing beside a teammate with the same injury, on the same table, at the same hours, with the same trainer. Whoever's back first will notice, and so will the coaches.

choices.label: Make it a team
choices.result: You push each other every day and swap the bad days. You both come back, and you've got a friend for life.

choices.label: Race him back
choices.result: You race him back and win by a week. He shakes your hand, and something between you cools a little.

choices.label: Compare notes
choices.result: Notes compared every afternoon: what hurts, what helps, what the trainers said. You both come back smarter, and a little closer.

scenarios.title: The Mortgage
scenarios.text: Your first mortgage, and the papers are thicker than your playbook: forty pages of terms, a stack of signature tabs, and a loan officer who keeps calling you 'the athlete'.

choices.label: Read every page
choices.result: Every page, read, with questions about the three that matter. The loan officer is surprised and fixes one clause in your favor.

choices.label: Bring {parent} to the signing
choices.result: {parent} at the signing, with reading glasses and opinions. He's done this before and asks the questions you didn't know to ask.

choices.label: Sign where they point
choices.result: Signed where they point, every tab, in twenty minutes. You hope for the best, and for a year you're never quite sure what you agreed to.

scenarios.title: The Family Health Scare
scenarios.text: A family member gets scary news from a doctor while you're on a road trip two thousand miles away. {parent} calls at midnight, trying very hard to sound calm.

choices.label: Fly home overnight
choices.result: A red-eye home, a day at the hospital, a red-eye back for the game. You're exhausted and glad, and the news turns out better than feared.

choices.label: Stay on the phone all night
choices.result: All night, on the phone with {parent} and the doctors, asking every question. By morning there's a plan, and you're part of it.

choices.label: Stay with the team and call
choices.result: With the team, calling every hour between meetings. It's the hardest week of your season, and {parent} says it helped to hear your voice.

scenarios.title: The Teammate's Divorce
scenarios.text: A teammate's divorce is playing out in the locker room: phone calls in the hallway, a lawyer at the facility, and jokes from people who should know better.

choices.label: Be there quietly
choices.result: Quietly there for him: rides, lunches, no questions. He says later you were the only one who never made it a thing.

choices.label: Keep the room kind
choices.result: The jokes stop when you're around, because you calmly make them stop. The room follows your lead, and he notices who did it.

choices.label: Keep out of his business
choices.result: His business, not yours. You keep out of it entirely, and he's fine with that, and you wonder sometimes if he needed more.

scenarios.title: The Charity Auction
scenarios.text: You donate an experience to a charity auction, a day at practice with you, and it sells for a fortune to a retired schoolteacher who has been saving for it for a year.

choices.label: Make it a full day
choices.result: A whole day: practice, lunch with the specialists, kicks on the stadium field. She cries twice, and so does {holder}.

choices.label: Do exactly what was promised
choices.result: Exactly what was promised, done well and warmly. She's thrilled, and writes the club a thank-you letter they print in the program.

choices.label: Bring the whole unit
choices.result: The whole specialist unit, recruited by you. She gets four for the price of one, and the punter teaches her to hold.

scenarios.title: The Brand Ambassador
scenarios.text: A sporting-goods brand wants you as its regional ambassador for three years: commercials, store openings, a signature cleat. The contract arrives with a pen taped to it.

choices.label: Sign for three years
choices.result: Three years, signed. It's steady money and a lot of store openings, and your signature cleat is ugly in a way you grow to love.

choices.label: Sign for one year
choices.result: One year, with an option for more. They agree, a little surprised, and you keep your freedom for the next negotiation and the one after.

choices.label: Pass on the cleat
choices.result: No contract. Three years is a long time, and the cleat really is ugly. A rival kicker signs instead, and you see his face at the mall.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Clinic Tour
scenarios.text: A kicking company wants you on a weekend clinic tour: eight cities, eight Saturdays, a thousand young kickers who all want to know what your secret is.

choices.label: Do the whole tour
choices.result: All eight cities. You see a thousand young kickers and remember being one, and you lose your voice in the sixth city.

choices.label: Do the dates near home
choices.result: The three dates near home, and your own training the rest of the time. It's a good balance, and the kids in your hometown are thrilled.

choices.label: Keep your weekends
choices.result: No tour. Your weekends stay yours, and you spend them doing nothing much with the people you love most, which is the point.

scenarios.title: A New Boss on the Sideline
scenarios.text: A new head coach arrives and doesn't seem to think kickers matter. In his first team meeting he forgets the special teams entirely, and the punter writes it down.

choices.label: Make him notice
choices.result: One practice at a time, you make him notice: the extra kicks, the clean operation, the timing. By October he knows your name and uses it.

choices.label: Ask for ten minutes
choices.result: Ten minutes in his office to explain what you actually do. He listens, genuinely surprised, and asks a good question at the end.

choices.label: Win the assistants first
choices.result: The assistants first, then the head coach follows. It takes a month, and it's the quieter way, and it works.

scenarios.title: The Team Leader Talk
scenarios.text: {coach} catches you after a meeting and asks you to speak up more in team meetings. 'They listen to you,' the coach says. 'You just don't say anything.'

choices.label: Speak at the next meeting
choices.result: At the next meeting, you speak: short, clear, about the special teams' mistakes and how to fix them. The room listens, and two veterans nod.

choices.label: Speak when it counts
choices.result: Only when you have something only a kicker can see, you agree. It happens twice that season, and both times it matters.

choices.label: Lead one on one instead
choices.result: Your way: one teammate at a time, after practice, in the parking lot. It's quieter and it works, and {coach} lets it go.

scenarios.title: The Team Trip Abroad
scenarios.text: The club plays a game overseas, and the trip is a week long: a different city, a different language, a different time zone, and a stadium that smells like rain.

choices.label: See the city with the unit
choices.result: The city, explored with the specialists: museums, a market, a terrible bus tour. It's the best road trip of your career.

choices.label: Keep your routine exactly
choices.result: Your routine, kept to the minute, even at four in the morning local time. It's lonely and very steady, and your leg feels like home.

choices.label: Shift your sleep a week early
choices.result: A week early, at home, you start shifting your sleep an hour a night. You land ready while half the roster stumbles off the plane.

scenarios.title: The Jet Lag Game
scenarios.text: You're kicking in a different time zone, three hours off, and your body hasn't noticed. Your leg feels like it belongs to someone who's still asleep at home.

choices.label: Follow the sleep plan
choices.result: The trainers' sleep plan, exactly: light, dark, water, no phone. By game day you feel almost normal, which is enough.

choices.label: Kick your legs awake
choices.result: Extra kicks the first morning, until your leg finally wakes up. It works, mostly, and you're tired by Saturday night.

choices.label: Sleep whenever you can
choices.result: Naps, whenever and wherever: the bus, the hotel lobby, a training table. You stop worrying about the clock, and the clock stops mattering.

scenarios.title: The Contract Bonus
scenarios.text: You hit a contract bonus on the last day of the season. Your agent calls to congratulate you and asks you, very seriously, to celebrate quietly.

choices.label: Put it all in savings
choices.result: The whole bonus, straight into savings, and you tell almost nobody about it. Your advisor sends a single word by text: 'Proud.'

choices.label: Treat the specialists
choices.result: A nice dinner for the specialists, on you, and nobody posts about it. {holder} gives a toast to 'the bonus we all earned'.

choices.label: Celebrate at home
choices.result: Takeout, a movie and a very long sleep at home. It's the quietest celebration in league history, and it's exactly right.

scenarios.title: The House Party You Host
scenarios.text: You host a team party at your new house, and by ten o'clock it's twice as big as planned. There are people in your backyard you've never met.

choices.label: Set the rules early
choices.result: You set the rules at the door: rides home, nothing stupid, done by midnight. Everyone respects them, and the night stays fun.

choices.label: Enjoy it
choices.result: Running with it, you enjoy the whole night. Half the team is in your backyard, laughing, and you've never felt more like one of them.

choices.label: Shut it down early
choices.result: You shut it down early when it gets too big. A few teammates grumble on the way out, and nobody calls the police.

scenarios.title: Your Old Coach Visits
scenarios.text: Your college special teams coach visits practice and watches every kick from the sideline, arms crossed, the way he did when you were nineteen and terrified of him.

choices.label: Spend the day with him
choices.result: The whole day with him: practice, lunch, the drive to the airport. He tells stories about you that you'd forgotten, some of them true.

choices.label: Ask for his notes
choices.result: His notes, please. He has one page, and one line on it is gold: your left arm drops on long kicks. You fix it in a week.

choices.label: Give him your best practice
choices.result: The best practice of your year, for an audience of one. He nods once at the end, which is the most he ever gave you.

scenarios.title: The Ball Boy
scenarios.text: A ball boy who's been at the facility as long as you have, since he was twelve, is going to college in the fall. He's the first in his family to go.

choices.label: Throw him a send-off
choices.result: A send-off in the equipment room, organized by the specialists, with a cake shaped like a football and a card everybody signed.

choices.label: Write him a letter
choices.result: A recommendation letter, written carefully over a weekend. He gets the scholarship, and sends you a photo from his dorm.

choices.label: Shake his hand
choices.result: A handshake on his last day and a wish of good luck. He'll remember it, and you'll wish you'd done a little more.

scenarios.title: The Scrapbook
scenarios.text: {parent} keeps a scrapbook of every article ever written about you, back to the peewee league newsletter. He shows it to you on a visit, a little embarrassed, very proud.

choices.label: Go through every page
choices.result: Every page, together, at the kitchen table, all evening. He tells you what he was doing the day of every article, and you listen.

choices.label: Help him digitize it
choices.result: A weekend of scanning, so nothing gets lost in a flood or a fire. He insists on keeping the paper one too, and you agree.

choices.label: Laugh at the old haircuts
choices.result: A few favorites, and a lot of laughing at your old haircuts. It's a warm half hour, and he puts the book back on its shelf carefully.

scenarios.title: The Fan Who Grew Up
scenarios.text: A kid who held a cardboard sign with your name at your first pro practice is now in high school, a kicker, and pretty good. His coach emails to tell you.

choices.label: Invite him to practice
choices.result: An invitation to watch practice, and a session with you after. He kicks better than you did at sixteen, and you tell him so.

choices.label: Send a message about the sign
choices.result: A message: the sign is still on your fridge. He posts it, and his whole school sees it by lunch.

choices.label: Watch his videos
choices.result: His game film, watched from your couch, with a smile. You don't reach out, and you check his scores every Friday.

scenarios.title: The Pet
scenarios.text: You get a dog from the shelter, a big nervous mutt with one ear up, and it changes your schedule more than any coach ever has.

choices.label: Love the morning walks
choices.result: The morning walks become the calmest part of your day. The dog learns to wait at the door at six, and so, somehow, do you.

choices.label: Bring the dog on Fridays
choices.result: Fridays at the facility, with the dog. It becomes the team's dog within a month, and the linemen fight over who gets to walk it.

choices.label: Build it into the routine
choices.result: The dog, built into your routine like a stretching session, with walks before film. Everyone's happier, especially the dog, who now knows the playbook.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Account
scenarios.text: Your advisor finally gets you to open a retirement account, after three years of reminders. The paperwork is waiting on the table, with little yellow arrows.

choices.label: Do it right
choices.result: Done right: every arrow signed, every question asked, contributions set to grow on their own. Your advisor sends a photo of the paperwork, framed, as a joke.

choices.label: Ask {parent} what he wishes he'd done
choices.result: What does {parent} wish he'd done at your age? It's a long, honest talk on the phone, and it changes what you sign.

choices.label: Sign the minimum
choices.result: The minimum, signed and then forgotten about. Your advisor sighs on the phone and sets a reminder for the same day next year.

scenarios.title: The Charity Basketball Game
scenarios.text: A charity basketball game with teammates in a high school gym, and you are, by a wide margin, the worst player on the court. The crowd has noticed.

choices.label: Play it for laughs
choices.result: Every miss, celebrated like a championship. The crowd loves it, the clips go around, and the charity raises more than it ever has.

choices.label: Practice for a week
choices.result: A week of secret practice in your driveway. You score twice in the game, and your teammates are genuinely amazed.

choices.label: Coach from the bench
choices.result: A clipboard, a whistle and the bench. You coach your team to a win, and the losing team demands a rematch.

scenarios.title: Supporting a Teammate's Cause
scenarios.text: A teammate is launching a foundation for kids in his old neighborhood and asks you to stand beside him. It's his cause, and he's nervous about it.

choices.label: Show up
choices.result: Every event this season, and you show up early to each one. He stops looking nervous by the third, and you help him with the speeches.

choices.label: Help with the plan
choices.result: You help him build the plan, not just the photos: a budget, a board, a calendar. A year later, it's still running.

choices.label: Donate quietly
choices.result: A quiet donation and your best wishes. He's grateful, and you can tell from his face that he hoped you'd stand beside him.

scenarios.title: The Old Rival on Your Team
scenarios.text: A kicker you competed with all through college signs with your club as a backup. He beat you for a scholarship once. Now he's the one on the practice squad.

choices.label: Bury the old rivalry
choices.result: Lunch on his first day, and the old rivalry turns into a joke you both share. By midseason, he's your best friend on the team.

choices.label: Stay ahead every day
choices.result: Ahead of him every day, by a little. He notices, you notice, and neither of you says a word about the scholarship.

choices.label: Help him fit in
choices.result: His introduction to the room, made by you, generously. The room notices how you handle it, and so does {coach}, who says nothing and remembers.

scenarios.title: The Brother's Wedding
scenarios.text: {sibling} is getting married on a game weekend. The date was set before the schedule came out, and {sibling} has already asked you to give the toast.

choices.label: Fly in for the wedding
choices.result: The Friday, granted by {coach}, a flight back Saturday night. You give the toast, and {sibling} doesn't stop crying through it.

choices.label: Help move the date
choices.result: A different date, found together with {sibling}, who moves it a week. You're there all weekend, and so is the rest of the family.

choices.label: Send a video toast
choices.result: A video toast, recorded in the locker room. {sibling} plays it twice, and you watch the reception on a phone in a hotel.

scenarios.title: The City Starts to Feel Like Home
scenarios.text: One morning you realize you know your neighbors' names, your barista knows your order, and the dry cleaner asks about your knee. The city has started to feel like home.

choices.label: Put down roots
choices.result: A neighborhood group, a library card, a farmers' market on Saturdays. You start saying yes to things, and the city says yes back.

choices.label: Enjoy it quietly
choices.result: Quietly, you enjoy it. Home is a nice word, and you don't need to say it out loud to anyone to feel it.

choices.label: Think about staying for good
choices.result: A question you've never asked: what if you stayed here after football? You start reading about schools and neighborhoods at night.

scenarios.title: The Sponsor's Event
scenarios.text: Your sponsor wants you at a store opening on your only day off this month. It's three hours away, there's a ribbon to cut, and the regional manager has already announced you.

choices.label: Go and do it well
choices.result: You go, cut the ribbon, sign for two hours and smile until your face hurts. The sponsor is thrilled, and your day off disappears.

choices.label: Offer another day
choices.result: A different day, offered politely. They take it, and reschedule the ribbon, and the regional manager pretends it was his idea.

choices.label: Keep your day off
choices.result: No, politely, and you keep your day off. The sponsor is a little cooler next time, and you sleep until ten.

scenarios.title: The Mid-Career Check-In
scenarios.text: Your agent takes you to lunch and asks a question nobody's asked you before: where do you want to be in five years? Not the contract. The life.

choices.label: Write it down
choices.result: The club, the house, the people, the life after, written on a napkin. Your agent keeps the napkin and brings it to every meeting.

choices.label: Aim for the top
choices.result: The top, you say: the best in the league, the biggest contract, the Hall of Fame. Your agent smiles and gets to work.

choices.label: Ask your family first
choices.result: Your family first, you say, and you ask them that night. Their answer surprises you, and it changes the next contract.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Gets Rich
scenarios.text: A teammate signs a huge contract and starts acting like it: the new watch, the entourage, the late arrivals, a new way of talking to the equipment staff.

choices.label: Talk to him as a friend
choices.result: A quiet word, as a friend, in the parking lot. He hears it, eventually, and apologizes to the equipment staff on his own.

choices.label: Keep the room together
choices.result: The room, kept from turning on him. You defend him in public and push him in private, and by December he's himself again.

choices.label: Let him be
choices.result: Money changes people for a while, you decide, and you let him be. He comes back to earth by spring, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Practice Squad Kicker
scenarios.text: The practice squad kicker is good, really good, and the coaches know it. They've started watching his kicks as closely as yours, and he's started noticing.

choices.label: Raise your level
choices.result: Your level, raised, and kept there. Every practice is better than the last, and the coaches start watching your kicks again.

choices.label: Help him anyway
choices.result: Help, freely given: his plant foot, his routine, his nerves. He'll get a job somewhere, and he'll remember who helped him.

choices.label: Ask where you stand
choices.result: {coach}, asked plainly where you stand. The answer is fair and a little uncomfortable, and you leave with a clear target.

scenarios.title: The Season-Ticket Holder
scenarios.text: A season-ticket holder has sat in the same seat behind the bench for thirty years, and talks to you every single week: weather, wind, his late wife's opinions on kickers.

choices.label: Learn his story
choices.result: His story, over a dozen conversations: he was here for every era of this club, good and terrible. You start looking for him before warmups.

choices.label: Bring him onto the field
choices.result: A practice pass, arranged by you. He walks onto the field for the first time in thirty years and has to sit down.

choices.label: Wave every week
choices.result: A wave every week, and he waves back from his seat. It's small and steady, and you'd miss it terribly if it ever stopped.

scenarios.title: The Charity Visit You Remember
scenarios.text: A charity visit to the children's hospital leaves a mark. One kid, eight years old, asked you to kick a paper ball across his room, and you can't stop thinking about him.

choices.label: Go back on your own
choices.result: Back, on your own, without cameras, twice a month. The kid's family remembers you forever, and you remember them every time you see a paper ball.

choices.label: Start something
choices.result: A small fund for the hospital, started by you and run by a nurse. It buys games, tablets and paper balls, and it's still running years later.

choices.label: Keep his drawing in your locker
choices.result: His drawing of you, kicking a paper ball, goes in your locker. You look at it before every game, and it calms you more than any routine.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Staff Dinner
scenarios.text: The coaches invite you to dinner at the head coach's house, which they've never done before. You're the only player there, and there are place cards.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: Dinner, stories and a long evening on the patio. They're people too, it turns out, and the head coach does a very bad impression of you.

choices.label: Go and listen closely
choices.result: Mostly listening, all evening. You learn what they think of the special teams, and what they think of you, and both are useful.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.result: A polite no. It feels strange to eat with the people who decide your job, and you're not sure that's a good reason.

scenarios.title: The Big Market Rumor
scenarios.text: A big-market club is rumored to want you next season. Your agent mentions it 'just so you know', and every reporter at your locker mentions it too.

choices.label: Let the rumor be a rumor
choices.result: Silence, and no comment to anyone. The rumor stays a rumor, and you stay focused on this season, mostly, and the reporters move on.

choices.label: Reassure your club
choices.result: Your own club hears it from you directly: you're happy here. The general manager thanks you, and the front office remembers.

choices.label: Kick like it's an audition
choices.result: Fuel, every single week: you kick like the big-market club is watching every practice, because it probably is, and your leg has never felt better.

scenarios.title: The Weather Delay
scenarios.text: A lightning delay in the second quarter, and the teams go to the locker rooms for three hours. Your leg is cold by the first hour and stiff by the second.

choices.label: Plan the warmup with the trainers
choices.result: A warmup plan, built with the trainers: bike, bands, a heat pack every thirty minutes. You walk out loose and ready when the lights come back on.

choices.label: Keep the unit laughing
choices.result: Card tricks, bad jokes and an impression of {coach}. The specialists laugh through the whole delay, and three hours pass like one.

choices.label: Rest in the locker room
choices.result: A towel over your eyes, a bench, and rest. You nap for an hour, and you're fresh, if a little stiff, when they call you back.

scenarios.title: The Players' Council
scenarios.text: The players form a leadership council after a rough season, eight players, and they vote you on. The first meeting is Monday, and there's already a list of problems.

choices.label: Commit to the council
choices.result: Every meeting, every follow-up, every hard conversation with management. The council fixes three real problems, and you lose a lot of sleep doing it.

choices.label: Bring data to every meeting
choices.result: Numbers, charts and dates to every single meeting. The coaches start listening to the council because of the data, and say so.

choices.label: Stay quiet on the council
choices.result: On the council, quietly, letting the others lead. You vote, you listen, and you're glad when the season ends and the meetings stop.

scenarios.title: Moving House
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} are buying a house, and every room becomes an argument about how long you'll stay in this city: a nursery, an office, a guest room for {parent}.

choices.label: Buy the house they love
choices.result: The house {love_interest} loves, with the big kitchen and the bad plumbing. It's the right call, and you know it by the first dinner.

choices.label: Buy something easy to sell
choices.result: Something practical, easy to sell if you're traded. It's sensible and a little sad, and {love_interest} agrees without much enthusiasm.

choices.label: Keep renting a year
choices.result: Another year of renting, and the argument waits in the corner. It's easier for now, and it will come back every time you pass an open house.
